messages:
olivia: Heads-up — ran a 100->2000 concurrency sweep overnight against the int8 quantized bring-up model (runner v2). Saw an odd latency plateau + cost spike. attaching quick summary.

olivia: TL;DR: p50 rises modestly, p95 jumps at ~800 conc, then CPU stays high and cost_per_token increases sharply after ~1200 conc. runner pod restarts observed at 1370 conc.

olivia: Command used: `./eval-runner --model redwood-v2-int8 --concurrency-range 100:2000 --qps 0 --batch-policy continuous --samples 200` 

olivia: Quick log snippet from runner (grep around restart):
```
2026-03-15T03:12:04Z INFO serving: accepting batch size=64
2026-03-15T03:12:22Z WARN runtime: KVCache wait_for_lock 120ms
2026-03-15T03:12:22Z ERROR runtime: encoder_lock wait exceeded, dumping stacks
2026-03-15T03:12:23Z INFO k8s: pod redwood-runner-5f4d restart
```

olivia: Cost math (cheap check): `jq '.tokens_generated|add / .requests' results.json` shows cost_per_token ~2.3x baseline at high conc.

sam_ml: ugh. two quick guesses: 1) our continuous batching policy might be hitting max-batch-window=> causing head-of-line blocking when KV cache miss rate increases. 2) quant int8 path might fall back to slower kernel for certain sequence lengths — check kernel selection logs.

sam_ml: can you paste the runner verbose logs? run with `--runtime-log-level debug --kernel-logs` if possible.

henry_infra: also check the recent infra change — I merged a semaphore tweak last week that changed the default kv_lock_timeout from 50ms -> 200ms for safer eviction. could be interacting badly with busy loops.

maria_prod: dashboard snapshot: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/runs/2026-03-15-load?orgId=1 — p95 chart annotated. note the aggregator metric for cpu-per-token was using a 1m rollup; that might hide early spikes.

eval-runner-bot: ci-job/runner-sweep-17678 failed: flaky-runtime-exit detected, restarted 1 time, sample-dump uploaded to s3://redwood-evals/1767832100/

olivia: attaching the sample dump id: s3://redwood-evals/1767832100/samples.tar.gz (contains requests.json and runner-debug.log)

sam_ml: quick reproduce step for infra team: `./eval-runner --model redwood-v2-int8 --concurrency 1200 --samples 500 --runtime-log-level debug` — focus on KVCache miss/evict lines and kernel selection output.

henry_infra: i'll grep the dump for `wait_for_lock` and `encoder_lock` and cross-ref with the semaphore commit. if this reproduces, we can try reverting timeout or add backpressure at the routing layer.

maria_prod: also noticed our p95 calculation in the perf-ci pipeline was using the wrong percentile function (we were doing weighted-average of buckets instead of exact p95 when bucket_count < 100). opened GH PR to fix: GH#1729.

ci-bot: perf-pipeline/17678 reported: p95_calculation_mismatch -> job marked unstable

olivia: proposed triage plan:
- sam_ml: grab kernel-selection logs + confirm if fallback triggered (owner: @sam_ml)
- henry_infra: run a focused reproduce at 1200 and check semaphore interactions; try revert/change kv_lock_timeout (owner: @henry_infra)
- maria_prod: patch perf-ci p95 aggregator and re-run historical sweep to see if the regression is an artifact (owner: @maria_prod)
- olivia: I'll re-run the sweep with `--batch-policy fixed:128` and attach results to compare batching effects (owner: @olivia)

olivia: can everyone ack and add any other quick checks? i want to avoid chasing a false-positive cost regression if it's only an aggregator bug.

sam_ml: ack. will try to reproduce locally with GPU mock + profiler. also will check for kernel fallback logs mentioning "int8-fallback" or "slow-gemm".

henry_infra: ack. will start with the semaphore revert test and post findings in this thread.

maria_prod: ack. if the p95 fix changes historical numbers, we'll generate a side-by-side report and label the old runs as 'computed-by-old-aggregator' to avoid confusion.

eval-runner-bot: upload complete: s3://redwood-evals/1767832100/runner-debug.log (12MB)

olivia: thanks — i'll wait ~2h for the initial reproduce results then decide if we need an oncall ping. :hourglass:
